title: Differentiation of Selected Biological and Synthetic Wound Closure Matrices in the Treatment of Burn Patients
summary:
This study investigates two different methods for treating deep burn wounds. After the removal of dead tissue (debridement), the wound is covered with a skin substitute to support healing.

Two already approved and commonly used materials are being compared: a synthetic material (SupraSDRM®) and a natural fish skin matrix (Kerecis®). Participants are randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups.

The aim of the study is to determine which of the two approaches leads to faster and improved wound healing and is more beneficial for patients. Both treatments represent the current standard of care and are routinely used in clinical practice.
conditions: All burns of grade II to III

interventions.name:
Intervention group (Arm 1):
Application of the synthetic skin substitute SupraSDRM® following enzymatic debridement in patients with deep burn wounds (grade II–III). Subsequent standardized wound care includes regular dressing changes and clinical follow-up assessments.

Control group (Arm 2):
Application of the fish skin matrix Kerecis® following enzymatic debridement in patients with deep burn wounds (grade II–III). Subsequent identical standardized wound care includes regular dressing changes and clinical follow-up assessments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients aged over 18 years
- ABSI (Abbreviated Burn Severity Index) score below 9
- Deep dermal burns (grade 2b) with focal areas of third-degree burns
- Confirmation of burn depth by Laser Doppler Imaging (LDI)
- Absence of severe comorbidities such as advanced heart failure or renal failure
- Stable hemodynamic parameters (blood pressure, heart rate)
- Notification of refusal of study participation by the patient’s legal guardian
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe comorbidities such as unstable cardiovascular diseases, severe renal insufficiency, or hepatic disorders that could compromise participation in the study.
- Multimorbid patients whose condition could interfere with safe participation in the study.
- Pregnant women, as the effects of the treatment on the fetus are not sufficiently known.
- Patients with severe psychiatric disorders or cognitive impairments that may affect their ability to understand and comply with the treatment or study protocols.
- Known allergies or hypersensitivity to components of the investigated wound closure matrices.
- Insufficient compliance or cooperation of the patient or their legal representative to participate in the study.
- Participation in other clinical trials that could potentially influence the results of the present study.
- Patients with isolated second-degree (2a) or third-degree burns.
- Withdrawal of consent or notification of discontinuation of the patient’s participation in the study.
